newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Liberalising Taiwan awards eight paging franchises.
newsitem.headline: Liberalising Taiwan awards eight paging franchises.

text.p: Taiwan on Thursday awarded eight licences to operate wireless paging systems in the island's liberalising telecommunications market, officials said.

Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd, which failed to win one of eight lucrative mobile telephone franchises in hotly contested bidding three weeks ago, came out better in the paging battle, sharing in one of two island-wide franchises.
Hongkong Telecom is a minority partner in a Taiwan consortium headed by First International Computer, the island's second-largest computer maker.

A partnership headed by Taiwan computer maker firm United Microelectronics Corp won two paging licences covering parts of Taiwan while a unit of shipping giant Evergreen Marine won one, officials said.
Officials said 32 groups submitted bids for the licences.

The mobile telephone and paging sectors are among several liberalised by parliament in January 1996 when it dismantled a decades-old state monopoly by opening them up for private and limited foreign investments.
Foreign partners are limited under the new law to 20 percent equity stakes in such telecom ventures.

Conspicuously absent from the winners' circle was an application that included U.S.-based giant MCI Communications Corp, according to a list of selected bidders released by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications.
The second island-wide licence was awarded to a venture called "Chunghwa International Paging service" formed mostly by Taiwan's unlisted companies, including Dah Yang Industry.
The ministry had awarded eight mobile phone operation licences earlier in January.
